tob-0004: A conversation between the warrior prince Arjuna and the god Krishna on the eve of a great battle. Krishna teaches Arjuna about duty, selflessness, and devotion, urging him to act rightly without clinging to the results. This edition uses Edwin Arnold’s classic English verse translation, which first introduced the Gita to Western readers in 1885. It is one of the most loved scriptures of Hinduism.
tob-10804: Oscar Wilde’s mother, Lady Jane Wilde, collected the folk tales, fairy beliefs, and old cures of rural Ireland in this rich volume. Her pages teem with banshees, changelings, holy wells, and charms against the evil eye — the living folklore of a peasant culture. It is one of the great treasuries of Irish folk tradition.
tob-4004: Erasmus lets Folly herself mount the rostrum in this keen-edged spoof of monks, schoolmen, and princes. Penned in 1509 for Thomas More, it laughed the late medieval church out of its smugness. The book became the wittiest shot fired in the Reformation age.
tob-9047-62704: The last volume of Pliny’s Natural History crowns the great work — the closing books on stones, gems, and the sum of his world-survey. Pliny died spying out Vesuvius’s blast, and his storehouse is his monument. Bostock’s edition bears the whole vast work to English readers.
tob-0104: This 1400s German hand-book is a working wonder-man’s vade-mecum — devil-raisings, treasure-findings, and spells for love and unseen-going. Its Latin, with rough pictures, shows wonder-working as men truly plied it. The manual is a rare leftover of medieval sorcery.
tob-9104: Hume’s Thirteen Chief Upanishads is the classic one-book English of Vedanta’s root-texts — the forest word on the Self and the All-One. His scholar’s hand made these deep texts open to all. Nachiketas and Yajnavalkya speak here in plain dress. The volume stays the standard English Upanishads.
tob-13504: This whole 1898 printing of Agrippa’s Three Books of Occult Philosophy gives the Rebirth magic-book uncut. It sets out star-lore, Jewry’s hidden teaching, and ghost-magic in one vast frame. The Victorian re-issue woke the classic for a new age of seekers. The books stay western wonder-craft’s ground.
cia-0000104904: A June 1994 document of CIA security guidance and procedures, laying out the everyday rules for protecting classified information. It covers the practical side of secrecy: how staff should handle, store, and talk about sensitive material. Issued just after the Cold War, it reflects an agency tightening its own house even as old threats faded.
cia-0000119204: An estimated November 1987 report on the sighting of a possible MIA burial site in Xieng Khouang province, Laos. Crash sites and graves in the Laotian highlands were investigated one by one. The entry shows the search for the missing extending to the most remote corners of Indochina.
cia-0000119704: A January 1953 study of Middle East conditions and trends affecting American security. Oil, new nations, and Cold War rivalry made the region a permanent item on Washington's worry list. The document is an early-1950s tour of a region that never left the agenda.
cia-0000124304: An October 1972 report on air raid shelters at Luta, Shenyang, and Shihchiachuang — the archive's spellings wander — plus Peking's subway and suspected sites. cia-0000132504: A February 1961 report, its title garbled, on Cuba's reaction to anti-Castro invasions. Exile raids were already hitting the island, months before the Bay of Pigs. The document shows Havana's defenses hardening: the revolution, braced for attack.
cia-0000132604: An August 1960 report bluntly titled Cuban Situation Worsens. Four words said it all — the embassy's view, darkening. The document is the verdict: the island, deteriorating.
cia-0000135804: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN with operational and general directive information. The headquarters spoke; the field listened. The document is the directive: the orders, transmitted.
cia-0000135904: A 1954 paper on acts of force before D-day. The pre-invasion violence — sabotage, intimidation, terror — planned in advance. The document is the prelude: the force, pre-authorized.

cia-0000136404: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN providing background on IDENs knowledgeable of communists — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The experts, profiled. The entry is the background: the knowledgeable, listed.
cia-0000136904: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on deception and confusion activities. The tradecraft, named. The document is the doctrine: the deception, practiced.
cia-0000140404: A 1955 document on hypnotism and covert operations. The mind-control manual's sequel. The document is the pairing: the trance and the tradecraft.

un-sc-res-1304: Security Council Resolution 1304, adopted in 2000 — aligned. The Council deciding. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1504: Security Council Resolution 1504, adopted in 2003 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.

cia-0000135604: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135604. The brigade's papers, another bundle. The entry is the bundle: the exiles, documented.
cia-0000136704: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136704. The training year's papers, amid the 1961 run. The document is the amid: the year, 1960 — the run, 1961.
plos-pone-0000004: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper on how transgenes — inserted genes — behave when targeted to the mouse ROSA26 locus, a favorite landing spot for genetic engineering. The researchers found that orientation matters: which way the gene faces changes how it expresses. The paper is the finding: the landing pad, mapped — the direction, decisive.
un-sc-res-704: Security Council Resolution 704, adopted in 1991 — aligned. The post-Cold War Council deciding. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d104: The ambassador in the United Kingdom, Winant, to the President, November 8 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 104. London's embassy reported. The cable is the embassy's: Winant, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d204: President Roosevelt to Generalissimo Chiang, November 10, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 204. The president wrote China's leader. The message is the fourth ally: Chiang, addressed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d304: The director of war mobilization Byrnes to the President, November 24 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 304. The mobilizer wrote back. The memo is the answer: Byrnes, reporting.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d404: The ambassador in Turkey, Steinhardt, to the Secretary of State — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 404. Ankara's envoy wrote the department. The cable is the department's: Steinhardt, to State.
the-thirty-years-war-volume-04: The fourth volume carries Schiller's narrative through the later campaigns of the Thirty Years War, as exhaustion and diplomacy begin to shape the peace. Great commanders fall and empires bleed in prose of tragic grandeur. Essential for understanding how modern Europe was forged in suffering.
history-of-the-revolt-of-the-netherlands: Schiller brings his history of the Dutch revolt to its close, as the young republic secures the freedom so dearly won against Spain. His admiration for a small people who defied a mighty empire shines through every page. A noble finale to one of the great stories of liberty, told by Germany's poet of freedom.
by-england-s-aid-or-the-freeing-of-the-n: G. A. Henty's boys' adventure follows English volunteers fighting for Dutch independence against Spain in the years 1585 to 1604. Young heroes join Leicester's expedition and learn war, honor, and history firsthand. Henty's rousing blend of excitement and education made him the favorite of generations.
arxiv-2605-08904: AI agents that improve themselves by searching huge spaces of strategies need a fair test. Xiaozhe Li, Jixuan Chen, Xinyu Fang, Shengyuan Ding, and colleagues introduce OPT-BENCH, a benchmark for the iterative self-optimization of LLM agents in large-scale search spaces. The 2026 paper measures whether agents really get better at getting better.
arxiv-2605-09004: Cosmologists simulate universes in boxes, but small boxes miss large-scale effects; the separate-universe trick fixes that. Dennis Fremstad, Julian Adamek, and David F. Mota build an emulator that super-resolves such simulations — cheaply predicting fine detail from coarse runs. The 2026 paper is computational cosmology.
arxiv-2605-09204: Backpropagation through long sequences is slow because each step waits for the last. Shaun Christopher Lee and Sangeetha Abdu Jyothi parallelize it with LBI — parallel scan backpropagation via latent bounded interfaces. The 2026 paper makes training on very long sequences dramatically faster.
arxiv-2605-09304: Writing a static code analyzer takes expertise; describing what you want in English should suffice. Amirmohammad Nazari, Sadra Sabouri, Wang Bill Zhu, and Robin Jia generate complex code analyzers from natural language questions. The 2026 paper turns plain English into program-analysis tools.
arxiv-2605-09504: AI security policy keeps aiming at models — but real failures happen in deployed systems, not in weights alone. Michael A. Riegler and Inga Strümke argue policy should target systems, not models. The 2026 paper is a position piece on regulating the right thing.
arxiv-2605-09804: Random tensors generalize random matrices; the joint distributions of their eigenvectors reveal the underlying geometry. Naoki Sasakura studies symmetric random tensors in serious depth. The 2026 paper is random matrix theory, tensored up a full dimension. It is probability in higher dimensions.
arxiv-2605-09904: Video large language models must keep objects consistent across time; TOC-Bench measures that temporal consistency rigorously. Junzhe Chen, Siyuan Meng, Yuxi Chen, and colleagues build the benchmark. The 2026 paper is video AI evaluation with a precise temporal stopwatch in hand.
arxiv-2605-10104: B-H hysteresis in itinerant ferromagnetism, derived from Chern-Simons gauge theory — magnetism's memory from topology. Kenzo Ishikawa develops the derivation. The 2026 paper is condensed matter with gauge-theoretic roots. It finds magnetic hysteresis in the gauge field.
plos-pone-0003404: Plant geneticists uncovered a flowering brake in this 2008 study of Arabidopsis. The Polycomb Repressive Complex 2, a gene-silencing machine shared by plants and animals, was shown to hold two flowering genes, FLOWERING LOCUS C and T, in the off position. The finding explains part of how plants decide when to bloom, a trait breeders care about deeply.
plos-pone-0003504: Developmental biologists found the delivery crew for a neuron protein in this 2008 fly study. Dscam, a membrane protein with a TM1 segment, must be restricted to dendrites rather than axons, and the team showed the dynein-dynactin motor complex hauls it there. The finding reveals the shipping system that gives each branch of a neuron its own protein identity.
plos-pone-0003604: Alzheimer's researchers Yang, Knowles, and Lu tested small-molecule protectors in this 2008 paper. Non-peptide ligands of the p75 nerve-growth-factor receptor blocked the neurodegeneration and synaptic damage caused by amyloid-beta. The drug-like compounds point toward treatments that defend neurons against Alzheimer's toxic protein.
plos-pone-0003704: In 2008, Kumashiro, Yokoyama, and Ishibashi watched monkeys copy moves. Japanese macaques imitated body movements better when joint attention was set up first through eye contact and pointing. The result ties social attention to learning by copying in our primate cousins.
plos-pone-0003804: Meneghini, Packer, and Nassi-Calò documented a citation gap in this 2008 paper. Articles by Latin American authors in prestigious journals collected fewer citations than comparable work. The finding exposes a geographic bias in how science rewards its producers.
plos-pone-0003904: In 2008, Resa-Infante, Jorba, and Zamarreño found flu's polymerase needs a local escort. The PB2 subunit's interaction with host importins proved required for viral replication. The host-dependent handshake is a potential drug target against influenza.
plos-pone-0004004: In 2008, Frobius, Matus, and Seaver found ancient body-plan genes in tidy order. Hox genes in a marine lophotrochozoan showed both spatial and temporal colinearity. The genes' order along the chromosome matched the body's head-to-tail order. The tidy colinearity extends this deep body-plan pattern to a major animal group.
plos-pone-0004104: In 2009, Takahashi, Yoshina, and Masashi linked a brain gene to body fat. The worm version of PQBP1, a gene tied to intellectual disability, steered lipid metabolism. Knocking it out in C. elegans shifted fat handling. The result ties brain genes to metabolic balance.
plos-pone-0004204: In 2009, Kim and Braciale compared mouse lung sentinels. Lung dendritic cell groups differed in sparking virus-killer responses. The airway crews varied in teaching young T cells. The ranking guides nose-and-lung vaccine design work. Knowing the best teachers focuses vaccine delivery.
plos-pone-0004304: In 2009, Wolfenson, Lubelski, and Regev watched cells grip and let go. The juxtamembrane cytoplasm shaped focal adhesion dynamics. The near-membrane zone tuned how cells sensed surfaces. The finding maps the cell's grip machinery. The work reveals the cytosol's role in cell-matrix sensing.
plos-pone-0357004: When governments fight disease with technology — apps that trace contacts or flag risky areas — the tools can treat some groups unfairly. This paper examines how discrimination creeps into tech-based disease control, from who gets flagged to whose data gets collected and used. The authors argue that fairness has to be designed into these systems from the start, not patched in after the harm is done.
plos-pone-0354604: Cigarette smoke damages the airway’s smooth muscle cells, and this paper read their full genetic response. Sequencing the complete transcriptome of smoke-exposed human airway smooth muscle cells revealed sweeping changes in gene isoforms and regulatory networks. The landscape pinpoints which molecular pathways smoking rewires — and which might be druggable.
plos-pone-0354304: Which machine-learning classifier actually wins on heart disease data? This paper reproducibly benchmarked four classifiers on a large synthetic heart-disease competition dataset. The head-to-head, fully reproducible comparison gives data scientists an honest scoreboard — and a template for fair ML bake-offs.
plos-pone-0347004: One fish name can hide many species. This paper uncovered cryptic diversity in Astyanax fishes of Colombia’s Magdalena basin, using molecular and morphometric evidence. The split species rewrite the region’s biodiversity map — and what conservation must protect.
plos-pone-0357404: Old DDT lingers in soil for decades, poisoning land long after the spraying stops. This paper compared two applied approaches using white-rot fungi to treat aged DDT-contaminated soil, and distilled the lessons learned. The fungi-based cleanup offers genuine hope for land that chemistry alone cannot heal.
plos-pone-0357904: PCBs — banned but persistent — still contaminate wildlife, including in New Mexico. This paper characterized the presence of polychlorinated biphenyls within biota found across the state. The contamination survey maps how far this legacy pollutant’s reach extends into living ecosystems.
plos-pone-0354204: Floods don’t break urban road networks linearly — failures cascade in complex patterns. This paper studied non-linear failure patterns in urban road networks exposed to flooding. The failure patterns guide engineers toward genuinely resilient street design.
plos-pone-0357104: The endangered páramo bromeliad Puya goudotiana hosts intricate root microbial communities. This paper characterized its root-associated bacterial and fungal communities. Understanding this hidden microbiome may prove essential for conserving one of the high Andes’ most striking plants.
plos-pone-0356904: Rotavirus vaccination reshaped — but didn’t eliminate — childhood diarrhea’s causes. This coastal Ghanaian study examined enteric pathogens in children under five with diarrhoea in a rotavirus-vaccinated population in 2023. The pathogen landscape guides treatment where vaccines have changed the game.
plos-pone-0355204: Capuchin monkeys hunt small vertebrates — offering a mirror on human predatory origins. This paper documented small vertebrate consumption by bearded capuchins (Sapajus libidinosus), drawing insights into the human predatory pattern. The monkeys’ hunting illuminates the deep roots of our own meat-eating.
plos-pone-0356604: Low back pain is the world’s leading cause of disability — and expert input might change outcomes. This randomized controlled trial tested the effects of musculoskeletal expert input on low back pain outcomes. The rigorous design reveals whether specialist involvement genuinely beats usual care.
plos-pone-0356004: Carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas and Enterobacterales are nightmare bacteria — but new drug combinations offer hope. This reference-laboratory study examined carbapenem resistance alongside susceptibility to ceftazidime/avibactam and ceftolozane/tazobactam. The susceptibility data guide last-resort antibiotic choices.
plos-pone-0355604: Wireless sensor networks for the Internet of Things need topology control that learns. FRLTC is a new topology control algorithm using federated reinforcement learning for software-defined wireless sensor networks. The federated approach lets the network optimize itself without centralizing sensitive data.
plos-pone-0355504: Living near noisy establishments might damage hearing — at the county scale. This paper examined spatial and temporal associations between physical establishment density and hearing difficulty across U.S. counties. The geographic analysis reveals the environmental footprint of hearing loss.
plos-pone-0354804: Finding salient objects underwater — through murk and distortion — demands sensor fusion. This paper developed underwater multi-sensor information fusion for salient object detection. The fused approach sees what single sensors miss in the ocean’s visual chaos.
plos-pone-0355304: Smart meters on harsh coastlines drift in accuracy — corroded by salt and time. This paper built a deep learning framework for predicting measurement error drift in these sensors. The predictive maintenance promises fairer billing and more reliable grids where the sea air eats electronics.
europmc-pmc2845804: Stopping yourself from acting on impulse depends on a patch of the right frontal lobe. This 2010 paper defines the role of the right inferior frontal gyrus in inhibition and attentional control. The authors combine brain imaging and behavioral tests. Their work pinned a core executive function to its neural home.
europmc-pmc2860504: Brain scans hold hidden hubs, and this 2010 paper offers a math lens to find them. The authors bring eigenvector centrality mapping to fMRI data, ranking brain spots by network weight. Their method spots key connectors. The tool gave neuroscientists a new way to read brain wiring.
europmc-pmc2896904: RNA-Seq opened a floodgate on gene activity, and this 2010 review surveys the deluge. The authors cover how the tech uncovers transcriptome complexity, from new genes to splicing tricks. Their overview explains what sequencing reveals. The review guided biologists into the sequencing age.
europmc-pmc2904704: Human mingling follows hidden rhythms, and this 2010 paper captures them. The authors track face-to-face contacts with wearable RFID badges at gatherings. Their data reveals the choreography of crowds. The work informed models of how ideas and germs spread.
europmc-pmc2921404: Gut germ surveys need solid methods. This 2010 paper details sampling and pyrosequencing methods for characterizing human gut bacterial communities with 16S sequence tags. The authors' protocol became a standard across labs. Their work underpinned the microbiome boom. Thousands of later studies copied its recipe for reading gut bugs.
europmc-pmc2962904: Mesenchymal stromal cells promise healing, and this 2010 review takes stock. The authors cover current understanding and clinical status of the cells. Their overview tempers hype with evidence. The review guides the field. Trial results so far are mixed but hopeful.
europmc-pmc2970904: Protein movies need true-to-life twist physics. This 2010 paper sharpens side-chain twist energies for the Amber ff99SB protein model. The authors' tune-up makes the movies truer. Their settings spread through sim labs. Drug modelers rely on these numbers daily. Better twists mean truer drug binding poses.
europmc-pmc2978704: Diabetes leaves a chemical fingerprint, and this 2010 study reads it. The authors chart blood chemistry shifts in diabetics using several lab platforms. Their fingerprint reveals the disease's chemistry. The work points to early warning signs. Doctors may one day screen with a single blood draw.
europmc-pmc3002804: Olives hide a healing compound. This 2010 review covers oleuropein, olive's bitter defender, and its drug-like effects. The author surveys lab and animal evidence. Their overview backs olive's healthy reputation. The Mediterranean diet leans on this chemistry. Supplements now bottle the bitter compound.
europmc-pmc3017804: Poplar trees carry a big NAC gene family. This 2010 paper surveys the NAC gene regulators in black cottonwood. The authors map the family's roles. Their work aids forestry genetics. Wood and stress traits ride on these genes. Fast-growing poplars feed the paper industry.
europmc-pmc3052304: Genome data needs decontaminating. This 2011 paper brings a fast scrubber for sequence contamination in genome datasets. The authors' tool cleans the data. Their software spread through labs. Human DNA often sneaks into germ samples. Clean data yields truer discoveries. Metagenome studies rely on the scrubber.
europmc-pmc3101904: An old sobriety drug fights breast cancer stem cells. This 2011 paper shows disulfiram kills breast tumor cells with stem-like traits. The authors reveal the repurposing trick. Their work spurred trials. The cheap pill beat pricey rivals. Copper boosts the killing power.
europmc-pmc6507104: Alzheimer's is the most common form of dementia, slowly stealing memory, language, and the ability to handle daily life. This review gathers what scientists know about its risk factors and what might protect against it. It covers lifestyle habits, medical conditions, and environmental influences tied to the disease, giving readers a research-backed map of where prevention efforts stand.
europmc-pmc6545004: Septic shock - the deadliest form of sepsis, where circulation and cells fail together - kills a large share of its victims. This systematic review and meta-analysis pools European and North American data on how often it strikes and how often it kills. The up-to-date toll gives hospitals and policymakers a firm baseline for fighting it.
europmc-pmc6562604: Healthy cells run cleanup crews - autophagy and mitophagy - that chew up junk proteins and worn mitochondria. In Alzheimer's, amyloid and toxic tau jam those crews, letting damage pile up. This review details how the two hallmark proteins cripple cellular recycling, and why restoring cleanup might slow the disease.
europmc-pmc6591304: Cavities and gum disease cost billions, yet the genes behind them stayed murky. This genome-wide hunt combined dentist records with people's own reports of dental trouble - and found the self-reports carry the same genetic signal as clinical diagnoses. The result validates cheap survey data for dental genetics and flags risk genes.
europmc-pmc6647104: Celiac disease - where gluten triggers the immune system to attack the small intestine - is far more than a food intolerance. This comprehensive review covers its tangled roots: genes, gut damage, tricky diagnosis, and the strict gluten-free life. It also surveys experimental therapies aiming beyond the diet.
europmc-pmc6650904: Chronic pain rewires the brain itself - not just the body. This research article reviews how lasting pain reshapes brain structure and function, and how those changes feed negative moods like anxiety and depression. Understanding pain's brain footprint points toward treatments that target the mind as well as the body.
europmc-pmc6666404: Type 2 diabetes creeps up silently - but blood and gut signals may betray it early. Tracking 106 people over time with multi-omics, researchers watched host and microbe dynamics shift toward diabetes. The study catches prediabetes in motion, revealing early warnings before blood sugar spikes.
europmc-pmc6682904: Spotting Alzheimer's early could hinge on microRNAs - tiny regulators floating in blood. This systematic review sifts studies of miRNA as Alzheimer's biomarkers: which signatures hold up and which wilt under scrutiny. The field is young, but a blood test for early brain decay is the prize.
europmc-pmc6685704: Tuberculosis treatment drags on for six months - and shorter cures keep failing trials. Pooling patient-level data from three pivotal studies, researchers dissected why 4-month regimens fell short of non-inferiority even as four-fifths were cured. The analysis guides the next attempt at a shorter cure.
europmc-pmc6729004: Checkpoint inhibitors unleashed modern cancer immunotherapy - and PD-L1 is a prime target. This review covers PD-L1-blocking drugs: how they release the immune brakes and which patients benefit. The therapeutic class keeps expanding, with new agents refining the attack.
europmc-pmc6735804: Skipping breastfeeding costs lives and money - but how much, exactly? A new open-access tool tallies the global price of not breastfeeding: lost child health, lost maternal health, lost economic potential. The numbers arm advocates with hard figures for a soft-sell cause.
gao-gaoreports-b-309604: A 2007 GAO money-law ruling with a modern twist: could the border agency spend its budget on credit watch for staff after a data breach? GAO said yes — guarding workers' good names fit the agency's purse rules. The call sets a small but telling marker on what counts as fair spending in the age of hacks.
gao-gaoreports-b-299904: Synergetics cried foul on a 2007 award, and GAO's ruling is the last word. The firm said the bid contest was mishandled; the call tests the charges against procurement law. Each published verdict sharpens the shared rulebook — what agencies must do, and what bidders can demand.
gao-gaoreports-b-309704: Tense games with budget language — GAO's 2007 ruling parses 'words of futurity' in the ATF's 2006 spending law. The call decides what Congress's forward-looking phrases legally unlocked for the firearms bureau. Fiscal-law rulings like this are where grammar meets the public purse.
gao-gaoreports-b-299804: TELESIS Corporation took its August 2007 contract dispute to GAO, and this ruling ends it. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call weighs the protest and decides. One more verdict in the public ledger of how federal tech deals must be contested.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1004: NASA's people planning earned a guarded nod in 2007 — GAO's report says the space agency's workforce strategy had improved, but moon-shot staffing puzzles loomed. The findings balance credit for progress against the hard math of hiring rocket scientists. Big dreams need bench depth.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-904: America's story abroad needed better research in 2007 — GAO's report says public diplomacy had to get smarter about studying its audience. The findings press for strategic, joined-up polling and analysis. Winning hearts and minds, the report argues, starts with knowing whose hearts and whose minds.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-304: The promised base-closing savings were inflated in 2007 — GAO's report says the fleet readiness center math did not hold. The findings deflate the rosy projections and demand fixes. The report is a reminder that shutdown savings are easy to promise and hard to bank.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-604: The next pandemic was a when-not-if in 2007 — GAO's report says efforts to delay the flu's arrival were underway, but spotting the riskiest nations stayed tricky. The findings blend epidemiology with geopolitics. The report reads now as a dress rehearsal for the real thing.
gao-gaoreports-b-299504: IBM took its June 2007 contract fight to GAO — two case numbers, one tech prize — and the combined ruling settles both. Big Blue said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the claims. When the industry's giant cries foul, the referee's answer carries extra weight.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-404: Russia's loose nukes were getting safer in 2007, and GAO's report says security at the nuclear sites had improved, though the long-term future was shaky. The findings credit the gains. The report warns that the guarded atoms needed guarding forever.
openalex-w7207583204: How should a university judge its teachers? This study looks at how the Federal Rural University of the Amazon rates its professors. The authors use the science of feedback, how people change what they do based on the responses they get, to test the system. They ask whether the ratings truly help teachers teach better, and they point out where the process falls short. A close look at one school's review system.
openalex-w7207613304: COVID-19 did not only attack the lungs; it also damaged tiny blood vessels, and kidneys were among the organs hit. This umbrella review, a synthesis of existing reviews, gathers evidence linking the virus's clotting and inflammation effects to acute kidney injury. Following strict PRISMA guidelines, the authors weigh outcomes, death rates, and the need for dialysis. A rigorous summary of one of the pandemic's less visible but serious complications.
openalex-w7204998204: Botany can feel dry on the page, but a garden you can touch, smell, and taste changes everything. This study tests the sensory garden at the Federal University of Sergipe as an outdoor classroom for teaching plants. The authors assess how the space helps basic-education students learn through their senses. A creative look at making plant science vivid in a country famed for its flora.
openalex-w7204693204: Use of strong mind drugs keeps rising in Brazil. This study looks at a neighborhood drugstore in Maringa, Parana, and counts which controlled medicines left its shelves, for whom, and how often. The authors read the figures as a sign of wider habits in prescribing. A local snapshot that speaks to drug policy across the country.
openalex-w7204536504: When police officers build their own software outside IT oversight, security suffers. This article studies shadow IT in the Parana military police: the risks of unsupervised systems handling sensitive data. The authors argue for governance and standards to rein in rogue tech. A cybersecurity-management paper about the dangers lurking in well-meaning workarounds.
openalex-w7204444604: Crohn's disease is a lifelong gut inflammation with no cure, but treatment keeps improving. This literature review covers recent advances in managing it: new drugs, better understanding of the disease, and better lives for patients. The authors survey a fast-changing field. A hopeful clinical overview for patients and doctors alike.
openalex-w7204197604: Brazilian law requires schools to teach Afro-Brazilian and Indigenous history, but mandates do not teach themselves. This article studies how art-based teaching, grounded in Vygotsky's cultural theory, can turn those laws into real learning. The authors show mediation making policy live in the classroom. A hopeful study of culture as pedagogy.
openalex-w7204254704: The brain's immune system may be driving diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. This integrative review gathers evidence on neuroinflammation's role in how these diseases start and worsen. The authors searched major medical databases. A neuroscience review of the fire inside the skull, and what calming it might achieve.
openalex-w7127983704: Before blocking uterine arteries, surgeons need a map. This study tested contrast-free MR angiography for charting uterine artery anatomy before embolization.
